body: I looked into this a bit, and it looks like this issue is caused by a GraphEdit child called `_connection_layer` that is being copied twice when copy pasting because it isn't marked as internal and isn't owned by the GraphEdit node. The documentation says this is because of "technical limitations" and I personally don't know enough about GraphEdit to understand what that means or investigate this issue further

IMO the editor shouldn't be duplicating non-internal nodes that are not visible to the user. (= nodes that aren't owned by the current scene)

It's trivially easy to make a tool script that has the same bug as GraphEdit here:

```gdscript
# Attach this script to a Node, select it in the scene tree dock, and keep duplicating with Ctrl+D.
# Every new copy will get one additional child even though they're not visible.
@tool
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	add_child(Node.new())
	print("Child Count: ", get_child_count())
```
This _can_ be considered a memory leak, since if you duplicate and then delete the original, you end up with more memory usage than before. Granted, tool scripts _should_ be marking such nodes as internal in the first place.

Addressing the above issue would be a better fix, _but_ if building upon GraphEdit's hacky non-internal connections layer node is more preferable... I do have a fork for this: https://github.com/chocola-mint/godot/tree/graph-edit-copy-paste

Basically, it waits until `NOTIFICATION_READY` to initialize `_connection_layer`. It will try to look for an existing Control node that is likely an existing connection layer node before creating a new one.

Perhaps it's because the node isn't owned by the scene, but not even the name of the node is preserved when copy and pasting. This leaves us with very little information to uniquely identify a connection layer node.

Anyway, it's super hacky and I don't want to make a pull request with it either, but it's there for others who might be interested.
